def compress(grid):
    """The grid without its frontiers: every row and every column that is one color throughout."""
    rows = {i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1}
    cols = {j for j in range(len(grid[0])) if len({row[j] for row in grid}) == 1}
    return [[v for j, v in enumerate(row) if j not in cols] for i, row in enumerate(grid) if i not in rows]

def upscale(grid, factor):
    """Each cell as a factor x factor block of its color."""
    return [[v for v in row for _ in range(factor)] for row in grid for _ in range(factor)]

def crop(grid, top, left, height, width):
    """The height x width subgrid whose top-left cell is (top, left)."""
    return [row[left:left + width] for row in grid[top:top + height]]

def trim(grid):
    """The grid without its outermost rows and columns."""
    return [row[1:-1] for row in grid[1:-1]]

def replace(grid, old, new):
    """The grid with every cell of color old recolored new."""
    return [[new if v == old else v for v in row] for row in grid]

def hperiod(grid):
    """The smallest p such that every row repeats itself every p cells: the grid's width if none is smaller."""
    w = len(grid[0])
    return next(p for p in range(1, w + 1) if all(row[j] == row[j - p] for row in grid for j in range(p, w)))

# one task's program: the one shape, cut out by dropping every one-color row and column, mirrored left to right
from lib import compress
def transform(grid):

# another's: every cell as a block whose side is the number of colors other than the background
from lib import upscale
def transform(grid):
    return upscale(grid, len({v for row in grid for v in row}) - 1)

le(grid):
    """Colored diagonal lines (each a band of constant i-j or i+j) extend: the whole grid is tiled by those bands' colors cycling with period = number of colors."""
    cells=[(i,j,v) for i,row in enumerate(grid) for j,v in enumerate(row) if v]
    percolor=sum(1 for c in {v for _,_,v in cells} if len({i-j for i,j,v2 in cells if v2==c})==1)
    percolor2=sum(1 for c in {v for _,_,v in cells} if len({i+j for i,j,v2 in cells if v2==c})==1)
    band=(lambda i,j:i+j) if percolor2>=percolor else (lambda i,j:i-j)
    n=len({v for _,_,v in cells})
    m=next(m for m in range(2,10) if len({band(i,j)%m for i,j,_ in cells})==n)
    seq={}
    for i,j,v in cells: seq[band(i,j)%m]=v
    assert len(seq)==m
    return [[seq[band(i,j)%m] for j in range(len(grid[0]))] for i in range(len(grid))]

def frame_border_fill(grid, fill=2):
    """Background cells on the bounding rectangle of the non-background (frame) color become `fill`; a background cell sandwiched vertically or horizontally between two frame cells also becomes `fill`."""
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    vals=[v for row in grid for v in row]
    bg=max(set(vals),key=vals.count)
    cells=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if grid[i][j]!=bg]
    if not cells: return [row[:] for row in grid]
    r0,r1=min(i for i,_ in cells),max(i for i,_ in cells)
    c0,c1=min(j for _,j in cells),max(j for _,j in cells)
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    for i in range(r0,r1+1):
        for j in range(c0,c1+1):
            if out[i][j]==bg and (i in (r0,r1) or j in (c0,c1)
                or (i>r0 and i<r1 and grid[i-1][j]!=bg and grid[i+1][j]!=bg)
                or (j>c0 and j<c1 and grid[i][j-1]!=bg and grid[i][j+1]!=bg)):
                out[i][j]=fill
    return out
'''
